beaconOwnerIs: Flap Guardian (BNB Chain), set in LeverBeacon's constructor -- never the deployer

supersedes.reason: Flap interaction risk report, findings 4 and 5, plus two defects found while testing them. (4) harvest now verifies the dividend contract actually took the WBNB, by balance rather than by a return value it does not declare -- stranded WBNB sits outside _nav and is unreachable. (5) deleveraging used _shrinkBy, which shrinks both legs by the same fraction and so cannot move leverage at all; where it landed was decided by how much of the tail redeem the health cap blocked. _deleverBy moves the legs by the same absolute amount instead. Also: the closing health check demanded an absolute floor after an operation that raises health, and at 3x leverage health is exactly 1.2000 -- the floor itself -- so a deleverage landing on its own target was reverted by friction, and a deep rescue that improved health greatly was reverted too.

retiredNote: Every address this project has ever deployed and replaced. Registering any of them with Flap would bind a token to superseded code. tools/check-docs.py reads this list, so a redeploy updates one file rather than a constant in the checker.

upgradeAuthority.LeverBeacon: owns the vault implementation; Flap Guardian
upgradeAuthority.LeverFactoryBeacon: owns the factory implementation; Flap Guardian
upgradeAuthority.note: Both beacons transfer ownership to the Guardian inside their own constructors, so the deployer never holds upgrade authority for a single block. Nothing else in this project has an owner, admin, or role of any kind.
